1.e4 e5 2.Nf3 d6 {No opening was a surprise from Tartakower. His knowledge
was encyclopaedic; he would sit at the board and play almost anything on a
momentary impulse. Possibly this Philidor was quite unpremeditated.} 3.d4 
Nf6 4.Nc3 {Solid development, avoiding the trappy variations beginning 
with Bc4 or dxe5. Next move Castaldi continues with the simplest policy - 
get out the pieces and then castle. If Tartakower had followed the same 
method, at least it would not have been a miniature.} 4...Nbd7 5.Be2 Be7 
6.O-O h6 {Tartakower deliberately defers castling. It soon emerges that he
has set his mind on a K-side pawn-storm.} 7.b3 c6 {Completing the Hanham 
set-up, which aims to operate with a solid centre.} 8.Bb2 Qc7 9.Qd2 g5!? {
It is true that some excellent wins have been obtained by Black using such
methods. (One beautiful example which comes to mind is the game won from 
Yates at the Hague in 1921 by Marco, a Philidor specialist.) But for the 
idea to succeed, it is essential that the centre be kept closed.} 10.Rfd1 
Nf8? {Probably a losing move already. No doubt the knight is heading for 
f4, but the momentary weakening of e5 gives an opportunity which Castaldi 
does not miss.} 11.dxe5 dxe5 12.Nxe5!! {The combination is based on the 
bishop at b2.} 12...Be6 
    ( 12...Qxe5 13.Nd5!! {Would leave Black helpless.} 13...Qxb2 
        ( 13...Qb8 14.Nxf6+ )
        ( 13...Nxe4 14.Bxe5 Nxd2 15.Nc7+ )
    14.Nc7# )
13.Nb5!! {The offer of the two knights in succession makes a combination 
of rare beauty. Tartakower refuses again. "Schackvarlden" suggested that 
Black could have escaped the worst by cxb5 (see line) but he would still 
be lost.} 13...Qb8 
    ( 13...cxb5 14.Bxb5+ N8d7 15.Nxd7 O-O-O! 16.Be5! Bd6 17.Bxd6 Rxd7 18.
    Bxd7+ Qxd7 19.Qc3+ +- )
    ( 13...Qd8 14.Qxd8+ Bxd8 
        ( 14...Rxd8 15.Nc7# )
    15.Rxd8+ Rxd8 16.Nd6+ Ke7 17.Ba3 )
    ( 13...Qb6 14.Nd6+ Bxd6 15.Qxd6 Rd8 16.Qxd8+ Qxd8 17.Rxd8+ Kxd8 18.
    Nxf7+ Bxf7 19.Bxf6+ )
14.Qa5! {Threatening Nc7+.} 14...Bd8 15.Rxd8+! Qxd8 16.Nc7+ Ke7 17.Ba3+ {
Quick debacles in the Philidor are not uncommon, but it is a surprise to 
find grandmaster Tartakower among the victims. /W.H.Cozens "The Lost 
Olympiad, Stockholm 1937", BCM, London 1985, p. 74/} 1-0
